verdict.line: You lose if Malphite uses Granite Shield and Brutal Strikes to solo-kill you before level 6, but you win the 54.2% of games where you stack Siphoning Strike through the poke and let Wither and Spirit Fire flip fights from level 9 onward.

brief.thesis: Malphite holds the lane and solo-kill edge early because Granite Shield absorbs your poke while Brutal Strikes gives him free all-in windows a level 1-5 Nasus has no answer for. Siphoning Strike's stacking damage and Soul Eater lifesteal only erase that deficit once you've farmed enough resets and unlocked Wither to shut down his attack-speed steroid. The 54.2% winrate over 262 games is a lane you survive, not one you dominate, until Spirit Fire's armor shred and a completed Trinity Force let your stacked Q start winning trades outright.

theirWindow.when: Granite Shield fully recharged, Brutal Strikes up
theirWindow.what: He trades for free here — his shield eats your poke and W buffs his Attack Damage and Armor, so hold your Q stacks and avoid extended auto exchanges until his shield breaks.

yourWindow.when: Right after he uses Brutal Strikes or Ground Slam
yourWindow.what: His shield is down and both W (14s cooldown) and E (7s cooldown) are spent — Wither him immediately and chain Siphoning Strikes, since Soul Eater lifesteal now out-sustains his reduced output.

start.why: 278-game sample shows a 55.4% win rate because the shield passive blunts Seismic Shard pokes and Ground Slam chip while you farm Q stacks.

boots.why: 54.2% pick rate and 55.6% win rate over 189 games — the cooldown reduction buys more Wither and Spirit Fire casts per trade window, which is the whole matchup plan.

core.why: Spellblade proc off Siphoning Strike and autos adds burst and movement speed to run down a Seismic Shard slow.
Amplifies Soul Eater lifesteal and Fury of the Sands' health drain, the exact sustain this matchup is won on.
More ability haste for Wither/Spirit Fire uptime, plus its attack speed slow directly undercuts a Brutal Strikes-empowered Malphite.

situational.when: malphite's team stacks extra crowd control around his ultimate engage
malphite rushes armor and keeps winning extended auto-attack trades off brutal strikes
you need more sustained tankiness and an attack-speed slow in skirmishes
the game goes long and you need magic resistance that scales with your stacking

runes.keystoneWhy: The on-hit heal and movement burst let you dodge Seismic Shard and Ground Slam while topping off health, stacking on top of Soul Eater as you farm Q resets.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport posts the best win rate of the three common setups (58.4% over this sample) — Teleport lets you reset after stacking Q on waves without losing tempo, and Flash dodges his 1000-range Unstoppable Force engage.

playing.title: Stack Q on everything
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike resets and grows permanently on a kill — prioritize last-hitting cannons and casters even off-tempo, since OP.GG's own tip is correct: stacked Q is what converts this into a 54.2% matchup.

playing.title: Dodge Seismic Shard
playing.detail: Malphite's Q is up every 8 seconds and steals your movement speed on hit — don't walk straight at him when it's available, since repeated hits are the single biggest lane bleed.

playing.title: Check Granite Shield before trading
playing.detail: His passive recharges whenever he hasn't been hit recently — if you haven't poked him, your first auto or Spirit Fire tick does nothing, so strip the shield before committing further.

playing.title: Save Wither for his W
playing.detail: Brutal Strikes is only up every 14 seconds and buffs his Attack Damage and Armor for the trade — cast Wither the instant he activates it to gut his attack speed and turn the all-in around.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire before extended fights
playing.detail: E's 12-second cooldown zone cuts his Armor, which raises your physical damage and lowers his Ground Slam damage since that ability scales off his own Armor stat.

playing.title: Track his ultimate cooldown post-6
playing.detail: Unstoppable Force has 1000 range but a long cooldown (130s down to 80s at max rank) — don't overextend for stacks near river or bushes until you've seen it used.

playing.title: All-in with R once available
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands' max-health drain and extended range from level 6 onward let you punish any trade he opens with Brutal Strikes, since your durability now outscales his burst.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample figures are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade windows are this brief's own tactical read.
